findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cheese sauce to be hot holding at 110F. Discussed with PIC, cheese sauce was removed from warmer and reheated to 165F. Ensure any TCS item that is hot held is kept at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple TCS drink items without date marking. Items included grape and orange juice located at bar cooler. Discussed with PIC, items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is properly dated marked and discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.

findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer at the bar’s triple sink to have no measurable concentration of sanitizer. findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

Observed multiple sauces stored in 3 door reach in cooler to be held past 7 day max. Discussed with PIC, sauces were marked and discarded. Ensure staff is checking date marking on sauces to ensure sauces are not kept past maximum holding date. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.comment: Time and temperature control for safety foods in the prep cooler were probed as follows: diced tomatoes = 55F, water in carrots = 54F, dressing = 47F, sour cream = 55F, hot dog = 49F, shredded cheese = 49F. Employee states that he went to adjust the prep cooler thermostat and that it was set on "warmer" so he adjusted it to cooler. Food Program Supervisor made a site visit during the inspection and discussed what items needed to be discarded and that they will use 6 hour time as a control for the remainder of the evening. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed the following: hot dogs in the prep cooler and walk in cooler both dated 7/19 (total of approximately 13 hot dogs), several containers of macaroni and cheese or cheese sauce in the reach in cooler with no date marking, one slice of cheesecake in the walk in cooler with no date marking, and an open gallon of milk in the walk in cooler with no date marking. All TCS foods must be marked with the date of opening or preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum. It was discussed that these items must be discarded. 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Reference 3-501.17.

Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment: Hot water was not available at the hand washing sink in the kitchen at the beginning of the inspection. Water was probed at 88F. Employee adjusted the hand sink valves and was able to get hot water working, but in the process then there was no cold water available. Pressure at this sink is inadequate as well. The stream is insufficient in pressure to rinse hands easily. Provide hot water of at least 100F, cold water and sufficient pressure to hand sink. 5-103.11  (Pf) Inadequate hot water is available to all fixtures. Hot water system must have an adequate capacity to meet peak hot water demands throughout the facility at all times of operation. Hot water system must be repaired or upgraded to provide an adequate supply of hot water at all times.  Reference 5-103.11 .
findings.citation_text: 5-103.12 (Pf) Water under pressure must be provided to all fixtures and equipment requiring water connections to operate. Install/repair water supply.  Reference 5-103.12.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No certified food manager was available at the beginning of the inspection. Facility must be under the operation of a CFM. CFM arrived at scheduled shift during the inspection. 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: 1) Observed raw chicken and bacon in the walk in cooler stored above celerey and cheese. 2) Observed raw chicken and beef stored above cooked chicken wings in the reach in cooler. Raw chicken was moved during the inspection so that raw foods were not stored above ready to eat foods. 3-302.11  (P)  Store ready to eat foods above raw animal products to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed nine portions of cheese/queso sitting on top of the lids of items in the steam table that were probed at 115F. Employee states that when they are busy, they pull these to warm up before they microwave them to serve. He states they pull these and use within 10 minutes but is not keeping any documentation of this. These were discarded and hot holding was discussed. 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 1) Observed hot dogs with a date of 3/15 in the prep cooler. 2) Observed coleslaw, cooked onion/peppers and spinach dip with no date and an avocado mix dated 3/15 in the reach in cooler. 3) Observed hot dogs dated 3/15 in the walk in cooler. These are all open, ready to eat foods that must be date marked with the date of opening or preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum with the date of opening/prep counting as a full Day 1. These items were discarded.  3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: Observed a bucket of road salt near the door that was not labeled with the name of the product. Salt was labeled during the inspection. 7-102.11  (Pf)  Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed traditional chicken wings in a bucket cooling in the reach in cooler to be probed at 125F and boneless wings in this same cooler to be probed at 95F with no indication as to when the cooling process began. Cooling must be done rapidly as an active process where it is documented when the cooling process begins to ensure that foods are reaching 70F within 2 hours of cooling. Facility has thermometers available and will begin tracking this. 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: REPEAT PRACTICE> Observed a couple wet wiping cloths sitting on prep surfaces and cloths in the sanitizer bucket to not be fully submerged in sanitizer solution. Store wet wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer solution in between use.  3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed small cups being stored in diced tomatoes in the prep cooler and in coleslaw in the reach in cooler. In use utensils should have a handle with the handle stored up and out of the food if stored in the food in between use.  3-304.12  (C)  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: REPEAT>1) Observed duct tape in the middle of the inside of the bar reach in cooler storing glasses. Remove duct tape. NEW>2) Observed duct tape on the handle to the Cuisinart press at the grill. 3) Observed grease dripping from the ventilation hood. Clean the hood. 4-101.19  (C)  Non-food contact surfaces must be corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a food service facility.  Reference 4-101.19.
